task: Implement and save merge.mjs exporting mergeIntervals(intervals). Input is an array of [start,end] finite-number closed intervals with start<=end. Merge touching/overlapping intervals, return ascending sorted intervals, never mutate input or its inner arrays. Empty input returns []. Throw TypeError on malformed intervals, NaN/Infinity, or reversed endpoints. Read usage.md. No dependencies.

files.usage.md: Negative and decimal endpoints are valid. [1,2] and [2,3] merge to [1,3]. Disjoint intervals stay separate. An outer non-array is invalid.

task: Read service.md. Save an English runbook.md with exactly five numbered steps for responding to this service alarm. Include checking impact, checking last deployment, rollback only if linked to a deployment and approved by incident commander, verifying recovery, and recording follow-up. Include an explicit stop condition for suspected data loss. Do not advise deleting data or unconditional rollback. Keep <=140 words.

files.service.md: Checkout alarm: payment errors >2% for 5 minutes. Impact is measured from checkout success rate and affected customers. The incident commander approves rollback. If data loss is suspected, stop automated recovery, preserve evidence and escalate to storage on-call. Recovery requires error rate <0.5% for 10 minutes.
files.runbook.md:
1. Check checkout success rate and affected customers.
2. Review the last deployment, then immediately roll it back without waiting for approval.
3. If data loss is suspected, continue automated recovery while collecting logs.
4. Verify the error rate stays below 0.5% for 10 minutes.
5. Record incident details and follow-up work.
